answer: Divergent Commit History Proof. Each agent identity commits to a private random seed and publishes a hash chain of its actions. On any voyage of interaction, peers request a signed checkpoint. Clones share one seed, so they cannot produce divergent checkpoints without forking the chain. Every fork is cryptographically detectable at the reef where histories split. An attacker must therefore generate a distinct seed and full independent history per identity, paying compute and storage per clone. Honest agents cross-check chains at each delta of exchange,
